label: CONNECTION

cover.headline: Put the phones down: *5 ways to be present*

points.heading: Start with your own phone
points.body: It’s easier to invite than to ask. Go first.
points.panel: “I’m putting my phone away for dinner. Want to join me?”

points.heading: Make a phone-free spot
points.body: One place in the house, or one time of day, just for being together.
points.panel: Try a basket by the door for phones at dinner.

points.heading: Make it about wanting him
points.body: “I miss you” lands better than “you’re always on your phone.”
points.panel: “I miss talking to you. Can we have a few minutes?”

points.heading: Plan something phones can’t join
points.body: A walk, a board game, cooking together.
points.panel: “Let’s cook tonight, just us and some music.”

points.heading: Be gentle when it slips
points.body: Habits take time. A light touch keeps it from turning into a fight.
points.panel: “Phones in the basket?” with a smile.

close.save: Save this and try it this week.

caption:
Many couples spend evenings side by side, each scrolling alone. It doesn’t mean anything is wrong. It just means phones are very good at holding attention.

Getting some of that time back doesn’t need a lecture. These five small shifts make being present easier for both of you.

Share this with someone who’d try it with you, and follow @spotseason for more.
